question: On random windows of 6-72 months in 1999-2024, do the two event-clock candidates (the reaction long-short and the N1 H5|all learner) beat a beta-matched market MORE OFTEN THAN THEIR OWN MATCHED CONTROL on the same window -- at three liquidity floors and three borrow rates on the short leg?

windows.generator: identical to RW1 draw_windows, so seeds are comparable across files

control: the identical pipeline on R4_placebo_offset40 -- same names, same construction, same costs, announcement dates shifted +40 sessions, so zero event information
headline: 240 random windows; at the tradable corner ($10m floor, 200 bps borrow) the reaction long-short beats its own control in 0.713 of windows (median 8.57%/yr) and the N1 H5|all learner in 0.58 (median 10.454%/yr)
verdict: DESCRIPTIVE, NO HOLDOUT. reaction_LS: CONDITIONAL -- 71% of windows over control (median +8.57%/yr) but 24% of 2016-2024 starts | N1_H5_all_LS: CONDITIONAL -- 58% of windows over control (median +10.45%/yr) but 46% of 2016-2024 starts
